newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Voting begins in Romanian presidential election.
newsitem.headline: Voting begins in Romanian presidential election.

text.p: Romanians made their way through early morning mist on Sunday to vote in a presidential election that could end a long period of rule by ex-communists.
More than 15,000 polling stations opened across the country at 6 a.m. (0400 GMT).
The elderly, fearing a rush later in the day, were among the first to vote in the run-off contest between incumbent Ion Iliescu and anti-communist challenger Emil Constantinescu.

A high turnout was expected among the more than 17 million people eligible to vote in the impoverished Balkan country. No reliable predictions of the result have appeared in what is likely to be a tight contest.

Iliescu came to power in the aftermath of the bloody 1989 revolution that toppled Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu and is bidding for four more years in power with a promise to maintain stability and promote cautious reform.

If elected, Iliescu may find himself isolated as his leftist Party of Social Democracy was ousted from government by Constantinescu's Democratic Convention bloc in parliamentary polls earlier this month.
In bitter television debates, Iliescu has played on the conservatism and fears of many Romanians and said a victory for him would protect people from the costs of social change.

Constantinescu has urged voters to hand him victory in his second bid for the presidency to end the influence of communism in the one Eastern European country that has not yet had an anti-communist at the helm.
He pledges a new era of clean government, better economic management and reforms to stop living standards in Romania lagging further behind ex-communist near neighbours like Hungary and Poland.
Exit polls due shortly after polls close at midnight (2200 GMT) should give the first indications of the result, with official figures trickling in throughout Monday.
